title: 4D530013-Blinx_The_Time_Sweeper.xiso.iso

arms.A: 46936c6a3d (master, PR #434 folded), no --env: whole-page TB invalidation, the shipped default
arms.B: 46936c6a3d, the same apk, --env HAKUX_TCG424_RANGE=1: range test plus per-page code bitmap. The env is the only independent variable.

runs: 4D530013-Blinx_The_Time_Sweeper.xiso.iso, --route survey (the route of titlebench's Blinx soak 1790467161-titlebench-2612887 and of pass 1), --seconds 540, --device thor, 3 runs per arm interleaved A B A B A B. Pilot = the first A and the first B. 540 s rather than titlebench's 420 s because `mark play` falls ~257 s into the soak, and 420 s leaves only ~130 s of window.
reader: python3 docs/lanes/tbflip424/playread.py <result ids>. This is tbchurn424/churn.py with the window anchored on the survey route's `mark play` line: mark play + 30 s to the end of the log. No mark = VOID. Per run: gfps = the median of the hakuX-perf gfps samples in the window; churn% = (jcus + rdus) / vCPU cpu over the [tlb68] lines in the window. Per arm: the median of its three per-run values. The survey route's span median is NOT read.
why_this_window: On Blinx the survey route is in the first stage before `mark play` (the START/A rounds pause and resume it). After the mark it only plays. Pass 1's frames show the stage under control from the first play frame on (0-0-y-1790433159-titleplay-p1-blinx/route-frames/110116-play.png onward). The 30 s settle is churn.py's own default, not chosen for this data.
baseline_on_disk: playread.py over tbchurn424's Blinx runs (older refs, 300 s, so only 7-9 [tlb68] lines in the window): A 7e6a4ac88a gfps 12 / 11.0, churn% 2.2 / 2.8; B 1d1251aa4b gfps 10 / 13.5, churn% 0.0 / 0.0. Pass 1 (a5b5b628f2, 420 s): gfps 15, churn% 2.3, 33 samples. The per-arm gfps here are 3-4 samples a run and decide nothing; they set only the scale, about 10-15 gfps.

legs.M0 (instrument): Every run has a `mark play` line, >= 20 gfps samples in the window, [tlb68] in >= 90% of the window's 2 s windows, and xx = 0. A's [tlb68] lines carry rt=0 only; B's carry rt=1 only. A run failing this is VOID, not zero: it is re-queued once on the same arm. More than one VOID run per arm stops the lane without a verdict. FAILS in a world where the route no longer reaches `mark play`, perf lines are missing, or the env does not reach the emulator (B shows rt=0).
legs.M1 (the counter moves; the falsifier): Per-arm median churn%: A >= 1.0, and B <= 0.5 x A. Per-arm median di/s: B <= 0.1 x A. FAILS in a world where Blinx gameplay spends nothing on the two #424 mechanisms (A < 1.0: then the arm cannot show a cost that trades against a saving, and the M4' result is inert; report it and do not flip on it), or where the range test does not engage (B's churn stays near A's).
legs.M4' (must not regress, on gameplay): Per-arm median gfps: B >= A - 1. And no run of either arm crashes: no `Fatal signal` or `FATAL` line in logcat.txt, and the window's last gfps sample is within 15 s of the route's `soak end` line (frames still counted at the end). FAILS in a world where the cost the range test adds on Blinx outweighs the churn it removes, namely ~33k invalidator entries a second (each answered under one page lock) and ~1.5x the slow stores. Then B's gameplay median falls by more than 1 gfps, which is ~10% at this title's 10-15 gfps.
legs.decision: Flip the default in hakux_tcg424_range_on() iff M0, M1 and M4' all pass. If M4' fails, do not flip: diagnose from cb/s, inv/s and slow/s, and report on #424. If M1 fails with A < 1.0, do not flip on this arm: report that Blinx gameplay cannot price the lever.

what_this_cannot_see: Self-modifying code that a spared block should have caught; the range test makes invalidation do LESS. This arm shows no crash and no fps loss on one title's first stage. The pgraph must-not-move check on the flipped binary is a separate step, done after the flip.
expect_note: EMPTY ON PURPOSE: a soak writes no captures, so there is no golden key. The legs are read with playread.py off the [tlb68], hakuX-pages and hakuX-perf lines.
